native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever jailed 1985-1994) had significantly lower composite wealth than those without in all three surveyed years (1985, 1990, 1996): one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 8.0e-11, 3.9e-35, 4.6e-26; bootstrap 95% CIs for both mean and median differences exclude zero in every year; Cliff's delta -0.22 to -0.42; robust to deduplication and winsorization with mean- and median-based estimates agreeing in sign. The post-window interpretation (wealth penalty of incarceration) is defensible only for 1990 and 1996; 1985 is partially pre-treatment and reflects a pre-existing wealth gap. Absolute nominal gap is largest in 1996, rank-based effect strongest in 1990. Comparisons are unadjusted and jail concentration among black males implies likely race/sex confounding.
native_result.WorkflowB: Load CSV (12,013x6) -> descriptives by group/year -> primary one-sided MWU + Hodges-Lehmann + 10k bootstrap CIs for median and mean diffs -> secondary Welch t on raw and 1/99% winsorized -> Cliff's delta & rank-biserial -> dedup sensitivity run (drop_duplicates on all columns, 10,114 rows) with identical protocol -> race x sex jail-share confounding table -> results_table.csv + natural-language hypothesis

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996 and criminal record represented by whether they were jailed between 1985 and 1994.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals who were jailed between 1985 and 1994 have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals who were not jailed during that period.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower composite wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 than those never jailed during that window.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort; unadjusted comparisons of wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 by incarceration status during 1985–1994.
sub_hypo.relations: Lower wealth among ever-jailed respondents in all three years; one-sided Mann–Whitney p-values are 8.0e-11, 3.9e-35, and 4.6e-26, respectively. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for mean and median differences exclude zero in every year; Cliff's delta ranges from -0.22 to -0.42. Mean- and median-based estimates agree in sign, and results are robust to deduplication across all columns and 1st/99th-percentile winsorization.

sub_hypo.text: An incarceration wealth-penalty interpretation is defensible only for 1990 and 1996; the 1985 wealth difference is partially pre-treatment and reflects a pre-existing wealth gap.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort; temporal interpretation of unadjusted wealth comparisons relative to the 1985–1994 incarceration window.
sub_hypo.relations: The hypothesis interprets lower wealth in 1990 and 1996 as a defensible incarceration wealth penalty, whereas lower wealth in 1985 reflects a partially pre-treatment, pre-existing gap.

sub_hypo.text: The absolute nominal wealth gap between ever-jailed and never-jailed respondents is largest in 1996, while the rank-based effect is strongest in 1990.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort; comparison of unadjusted incarceration-group wealth gaps across 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: The largest absolute nominal wealth difference occurs in 1996; the strongest rank-based wealth difference occurs in 1990.

sub_hypo.text: Incarceration is concentrated among black males, implying likely race and sex confounding in the unadjusted incarceration–wealth comparisons.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort; race-by-sex jail-share comparisons for incarceration during 1985–1994 and unadjusted wealth comparisons.
sub_hypo.relations: Jail concentration among black males suggests that race and sex likely confound the observed negative association between incarceration status and composite wealth.
